steps: Measure the transmission of the chosen mid-IR fibre over the planned link length, or plan the analyzer close to the measurement point.
Prepare lab oil‑water mixtures covering the expected water range (e.g., [to be agreed with the customer]).
Measure each mixture with the NIR transmission probe and with the MIR‑ATR probe (lab reference).
Develop separate chemometric calibration models (e.g., PLS) for each method using the same reference water values.
Validate each model on held‑out mixtures and assess prediction error, detection limit, and response time.
Then measure in-line or in a pilot set-up against the reference method.
Select the method that meets the agreed performance criteria with the simplest hardware.
feasibility.decisionBasis: Performance (error, detection limit, speed) demonstrated on independent validation samples will decide which method proceeds to in‑line deployment. Agree two things separately with the customer before the test: the model accuracy required against the reference method, and the alarm or action threshold applied to the measured value.
